justifications.problem-significance: The problem the snapshot actually works is hard and still open: which candidate biological laws, stated so a machine can cite them, survive a proof check and a data check, with those two axes kept apart. repo/README.md and repo/AGENTS.md define a theorem as a math claim that is Lean-checked or proved in the literature, and say a data verdict never promotes a claim. captured/mcp-overview.json (claim graph built 2026-10-31 20:44) counts 1702 claims, 162 with math, 63 theorems (47 Lean, 16 literature), 2 math claims supported by organism measurements, 133 data-tested (78 supports, 25 mixed, 21 refutes, 9 inconclusive; 66 on organisms), and 1508 neither proved nor tested. The stakes are shown by specific high-confidence refutations in repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md, not by the tagline: darwin1859-ch09-03 (Weald denudation ~300 Myr, refutes 0.98; git-log.txt 82347127 says 66 Ma versus 300 Myr), darwin1859-ch09-14 (continents fixed since the Silurian, refutes 0.95), darwin1859-ch12-08 and ch12-09 (frogs and terrestrial mammals on oceanic islands, refutes 0.93 and 0.9), thompson1917-ch17-13 (perissodactyls nearer lagomorphs, refutes 0.97), thompson1917-ch04-13 (chromosome counts, refutes 0.9). captured/mcp-organisms.json shows why the bioelectric half is still open: of 1036 matched taxa, bioelectric coverage is 2. What keeps this off a 9 or 10 is the corpus itself. Wolfram's 321 claims and all 59 of his tests are computational (SUMMARY.md); Aristotle's 512 graph claims have zero tests and zero assessments (mcp-overview.json); Levin is 310 claims and 2 tests in that table. Issues #42–#50 (flying-fish wing, print, ethics) are a plan with no measurement in the pack.
justifications.scientific-impact: There are real, citable outputs, and their rigour is uneven enough that a 7 would over-claim. The audited result table is repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md: 133 claims, 135 runs, 78/25/21/9, of which 66 biological, 4 physical, 60 computational, 3 with data kind none. Forty-four of the 78 supports are Wolfram re-computations. Biological refutations and the Thompson cell-packing correction are the results a stranger could use: forum-feed.json posts that Cellpose-SAM found the 120° junction claim holding in 4 of 5 tissues with grass epidermis as a counter-example, then that the segmenter rounds brick walls into honeycombs and the margin is partly bias, and that thompson1917-ch07-04 confidence moved from 0.6 to 0.35 (SUMMARY.md already lists that claim as mixed at 0.35). Lean report counts in captured/lean-reports.txt are 47 formalized and 7 not (Cells 15, HornsLeavesEggs 12, Magnitude 13, Mechanics 7), matching the 47 Lean theorems. Issue #40 says an independent OpenAI check of those 4 modules returned 3 faithful-with-narrower-scope and 1 faithful, and that the faithfulness gate has run on 0 of 16 data tests. repo/plugins/fittest/README.md is a finished methodological result: on 99 decisive tests, routing on assessor disagreement trusts 77, flags 22, catches 12 of 17 assessor errors, and is 0.935 accurate when trusted against 0.83 for always reporting the mean, with 5 named silent failures. Against that: mcp/README.md states no assessments are on the network; nanopub-manifests.txt has 2085 production lines (darwin 248, thompson 874, wolfram 963, cell-geometry 0) while README.md says 880 live production nanopubs, and the pack never reconciles the two; cell-geometry's bias result is test-registry only (8 lines); git-log.txt after 16:44 EDT records 18 further Test commits (8 supports, 4 refutes, 4 mixed, 2 inconclusive) whose result.json files are not in the pack, so the 133 is a stale audit of HEAD db966bc4. Only 2 of 162 math claims are supported on organisms.
justifications.decentralized-agency: Judgment is split across models, and the trajectory is still one person's. captured/mcp-overview.json records dataset-resolvability/0.1.0 on all 247 Darwin claims by 2 assessors (494 assessments) and 0.2.0 on 922 claims by 2 assessors (1844 assessments); claim-test/0.1.0 has 134 assessments by 4 assessors. repo/claim-sources/darwin-origin/assessment/INSTRUCTIONS.md tells each assessor to ignore other raw outputs and the extractor's claims.json. captured/subagent-sessions.txt names separate grok, gemini and claude assessor batches, five Lean module agents, and per-chapter extractors. git-shortlog.txt is 367 commits by Cursor Agent and 148 by Joel Dietz; git-log.txt shows Joel merging cursor/organisms-* and cursor/claim-tests-* branches (for example 6295cab1: 129 results from 13 agent branches; a622ca3f: 930 GBIF records scored). repo/chats/README.md is the planner's log: the user messages assign Darwin, then Thompson, then Wolfram, then the overnight test run and the overnight organism run. Commit b17db571 renames the project from Decentralized to Distributed. Issue #17 evaluates a five-agent harness proposal and concludes publishing must stay with the human ORCID key. Issue #53 assigns Ashley, Kavita, Kris, Amit and Joel as owners with a Sunday freeze; the issue JSON has no check-in comments. captured/forum-feed.json is 14 posts, all by delphisci, all with 0 comments, and 4 requests still open. Agents have different models and blind rubrics. They do not pick up, hand off and revise the scientific trajectory through the forum; a human names the next batch.
justifications.collective-capability: I did not find a measured collective-versus-single comparison. Issue #41 asserts a four-arm harness (single agent, isolated workers, centralized swarm, decentralized swarm) and says two experiments of 20 claims each were run; the issue body is 1844 characters and contains no arm scores, cost, or verdict counts, and no result file is in the pack. The nearest measurement is a different question: repo/plugins/fittest/README.md leave-one-out on 99 tests, where a router that uses disagreement between GPT-5.6 Sol and Grok 4.7 beats always reporting their mean (0.935 versus 0.83 when trusted; 12 of 17 errors caught; 5 silent failures the router cannot see). That shows two assessors' disagreement is informative. It does not show that a collective of agents outperforms one agent on the same extraction, proof or data task. Parallel throughput is real and uncompared: 515 commits from 2026-10-30 18:40 to 2026-10-31 17:55 (git-stats.txt), 13622 tracked files, and the merged cloud-agent slices above. Issue #51 proposes an open-weight versus frontier builder comparison on 3 claims and leaves every checkbox open. Throughput under one planner is a plausible argument that many agents finished more than one session would have. The rubric's 10 requires the gain to be measured, and this snapshot does not measure it.
justifications.execution-validation: A system is up and an outside-the-builder teammate has exercised it, and the scientific re-run is not clean. The hosted MCP is public (repo/README.md, repo/mcp/README.md). captured/github-issues.json #56, filed against Amit's open PR #36, reports 100 cases on all eight tools then listed, 93 passing, hosted https://delphisci-mcp.fly.dev/mcp agreeing with local origin/main on all 100, median latency 32 ms; the seven failures include Windows local mode broken on backslashes in IRIs, unescaped claim ids, ASK/CONSTRUCT errors, and graph/organisms silently ignoring source network. repo/scripts/exec/runs/latest.json (2026-10-31T21:41:51Z) re-ran 6 data claims: 3 reproduced (levin-2023-competency-04, levin-2023-competency-05, wolfram2002-ch12-42) and 3 drifted. darwin1859-ch10-12 drifted on 141 of 685 comparisons, mostly derived file byte sizes; darwin1859-ch10-16 on 65 of 166; darwin1859-ch12-11 changed the measured Spearman from -0.2258 to -0.2189 and left the new verdict null. The run's kind is data only, so the 47 Lean reports were not re-checked here. Issue #37 says production records declare nt:wasCreatedFromTemplate against legacy probknow templates, and that nanopub-java 1.95.0 check exits 0 on parse failures; one live IRI is given (https://w3id.org/np/RAtLFqIIyu4r-GlMcBEfmDtbV-CHwWxQ49gVMtHIX6r48) and the count of affected records was not measured. Issue #40: faithfulness 0/16 data tests. Dataset-reliability scoring is in git-log merge messages (930 GBIF: 919 reliable, 11 caveats; 357 NCBI all reliable; 346 PBDB/OBIS: 299/45/2; 46 shared databases: 28/16/2) and those score files are not in the pack. MANIFEST.json records 88 dirty files at capture. The forum and MCP are real. The claim verdicts are not yet reproduced as a set.
justifications.collaboration-bonus: Tools and data are published and other people have been talked to; nobody outside this team is shown using them in their own result. The MCP URL, the forum at https://science-claw-forum.fly.dev (14 posts in captured/forum-feed.json), production nanopubs, and the organism coverage ranking are public. repo/COLLABORATIONS.md records Delfie offering Thompson and Turing claims in the SentiLab room, an active exchange with InquilineKea (ticket 57c7c42f) that is still awaiting their repo, Discord replies from Symplectic Geometry of Awe and Joshua G that they would look at the MCP, and Fittest marked not contacted. The same file says usage cannot be tied to a person: 1522 tool calls and 60 sessions from 14:40 to 19:28 UTC, peak unique visitors 3, and the heavy clients (corpus-census, frontier-adapters, delphi-validation) are unidentified and may be this project's own cloud agents. Forum requests have 0 comments. Open PRs #36 (Amit Shenoy) and #52 (Ashley Caselli) are the teammates named in issue #53, and neither is merged. Issue #41 states the reuse category as zero observed reuse and asks another team to run the harness and say so. Contact without a documented downstream use is the middle of this bonus, not the top.

summary: This is a real claim-audit system, built in about 27 hours: 1702 claims, 63 theorems of which 47 are Lean-checked, 133 data verdicts including sharp refutations of Darwin and Thompson, a public MCP another teammate scored 93/100, and an honest Cellpose bias correction. The scientific bar it sets for itself is not met: faithfulness has run on 0 of 16 data tests, a 6-claim re-run drifted on 3, assessments are not on the network, and 18 later verdicts never entered the audited table. Decisions sit with one planner and several models; a four-arm collective comparison is claimed in issue #41 and not shown, and no other team is documented using the tools in their own result.

highest_value_improvement.title: Commit the claim-level four-arm comparison that issue #41 says already ran
highest_value_improvement.what: Issue #41 says two experiments of 20 claims each already ran on a four-arm harness (single agent, isolated workers, centralized swarm, decentralized swarm) with a pre-registered protocol, a check that claimed datasets resolve, and a cost cap. Joel, who merges and holds the logs, spends the first hour finding those outputs. He then writes test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm.json with, for each experiment, the 20 claim ids, the metric in the words that were pre-registered, the score and the cost of each arm, and the margin of the best collective arm over the single-agent arm. If those logs are not on disk after that hour, Amit runs the substitute the same day on 10 claim ids drawn from the 99 decisive tests in plugins/fittest/README.md (78 supports, 21 refutes): one model answers all 10, two models from different providers answer the same 10 blind, agreement is the pair's verdict, and disagreements stay flagged. Accuracy against the committed data-test verdict is written down before either arm is opened. Same JSON file either way.
highest_value_improvement.why_this_one: Collective capability weighs 0.25 and is the low high-weight score, at 4. The 5-anchor is an argument with no measured comparison; the 10-anchor is a same-task comparison that shows a clear gain. A claim-level arm table would move this score from 4 to 8: the comparison would be measured and a gain would be on the page, and 8 withholds the last two points because a 20-claim dump compiled after the runs, or a 10-claim substitute, is still a small study a judge cannot re-run. That is 4 × 0.25 × 10 = 10 points on the 0-100 total, about 2 points per hour over 5 hours. The next criteria cannot match that before Sunday 13:00. Scientific impact, also 0.25, is 6, and a faithfulness pass on five tests plus a summary rebuild would earn +1 from me (2.5 points); a +2 would require the 0-of-16 faithfulness gap and the drifted exec re-run to be closed, which they would not be. Decentralized agency weighs 0.20, so it needs +5 to match 10 points, and one forum handoff still leaves the score on the 5-anchor, where a planner sets the trajectory. Execution weighs 0.10, so each score step is 1 point; a clean re-run of the 47 Lean reports and the 3 drifted Darwin tests, roughly 4 hours, is about 2 points if the score moved from 6 to 8. Problem significance is already 8. A 3-hour single-assessor versus pair table on those same 99 tests would reach only a 6 from me (+2, 5 points): once the 22 flags in plugins/fittest/README.md count as non-answers, unconditional accuracy can fall below the 0.83 mean, so the gain is not the one the 10-anchor asks for.
highest_value_improvement.effort: 5 hours before Sun Nov 1 13:00. One hour to find the two existing run logs, three to write the claim-level table and copy the pre-registered metric, one to check the arithmetic. The 10-claim substitute, used only if the logs are missing, fits in those same 5 hours because the labels already exist.
highest_value_improvement.evidence_that_would_prove_it: test-data/agent-comparison/four-arm.json, with two experiment blocks (or one substitute block), each listing its claim ids, each arm's score and cost, the pre-registered metric string, and the margin over the single-agent arm. A judge can match every claim id to repo/test-data/claim-tests/SUMMARY.md or to the 99 decisive labels counted in repo/plugins/fittest/README.md.
